decisions.statement: Entering a hold hands back the handle exiting needs.
A snapshot counts the holds entered and not yet exited.
Two holds entered at the same millisecond are two holds.
Exiting a handle already exited changes nothing.
Exiting a handle the registry never entered changes nothing.
A snapshot of an empty registry reports the oldest age as null rather than zero.
A snapshot ages the oldest hold from the earliest start still held.
The oldest hold is found in any order the holds were entered in.
An age is never below zero.
A hold never exited is held for the life of the process.
A caller that enters a hold exits that hold on the paths a request can end by.
Nothing here knows the request a hold is waiting on.

definition: what a gateway is holding open, counted and aged
